Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Pro

x64

_No response_

No

### Expected Behavior

Using the Node fs module's [cp methods](https://nodejs.org/api/fs.html#fspromisescpsrc-dest-options) (`cp`, `promises.cp`, `cpSync`, stable as of Node 22.3.0) to copy folders out of an ASAR works correctly.

It fails with ENOENT, e.g. `Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, opendir 'C:\Users\ben\AppData\Local\MyApp\app-3.32.0-r13901\resources\app.asar\new-folder-template'`.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://github.com/bendemboski/electron-node-fs-cp

### Additional Information

I appears the `cp` methods aren't wrapped is the asar fs wrappers?

nodes.title: Decide TypeScript support in preloads since v40
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Node.js has enabled TypeScript type stripping by default in v24 of the runtime and mark it as stable in v25.2. It means that Electron v40 would support this feature by default too. But as soon as Electron has custom loader for preload scripts which has partial Node.js (CommonJS) semantic it should be decided whether enable type stripping in preloads or not. In my opinion not having TypeScript enabled could lead to unwanted inconsistency in the code, which is run on Electron's side. Today there are three modifications of JS which developers should use in Electron: 1. Node.js (CommonJS, ESModules), 2. Electron's Preload Scripts 3. Chromium's JS (in webpages and extensions). With partial TypeScript support the difference between them would grow further

In my opinion it could be confusing for developers too as soon as they see `require` in preload scripts and decide it is a Node.js/CommonJS module, which has TypeScript support

Another problem is that it would lead to unexpected behavior when `webPreferences.nodeIntegration` is turned on and node integration would work differently

Also it would make users to keep using builder for preloads (when it's not needed for main code), what looks excessive

### Proposed Solution

TypeScript stripping should be enabled in preload scripts. It should be done in the same way it realized in Node.js to reduce inconsistencies in bahavior. It also would reduce the amount of software needed to run Electron with TypeScript

### Alternatives Considered

Leave TypeScript enabled in main code and use preloads in its current view

### Additional Information

_No response_

No

### Expected Behavior

When clicking notification created with electron Notification object, on Windows, "click" event should be triggered when the notification is in notification center.

### Actual Behavior

When clicking notification created with electron Notification object, on Windows, "click" event is not triggered when the notification is in notification center.

Wait until the notification disappears from desktop and is available in notifications center, or enable "do not disturb" mode" in order to have the notification directly in the notification center.

nodes.title: Clarify default Linux runtime dependencies
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

My company is building a couple of Electron apps, packaged with electron-builder, targeting multiple platforms, among them Linux. The apps  install (from both deb and rpm) and work fine on multiple Linux distros. When testing on RHEL10, however, we noticed that we get an error during installation of the rpm:

```
Error: 
 Problem: conflicting requests
  - nothing provides libXScrnSaver needed by XXX from @commandline
```

This is caused by electron-builder defaulting the dependencies for rpm to include libXScrnSaver, which is no longer installed by default in RHEL10 and in fact is not even available anymore.

Redefining the dependencies to be the ones listed in electron-builder docs as default, minus libXScrnSaver, seem to work fine. The rpm now installs and the app runs, and even `powerMonitor.getSystemIdleTime()`, which I understood to be the reason for why libXScrnSaver is required, seems to be working. There does not appear to be any `libXss.so.*` anywhere in the system either so it really does seem like this library is not needed.

Further, checking what libs are needed using readelf -d shows a bunch of libraries, but not `libXss.so.*`.

This begs the question, is libXScrnSaver actually needed anymore? And what are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux? I was trying to find this information, but was unable to.

Asking this in the electron-builder project I got this answer:

> This might be a better question to ask in upstream electron project.
> 
> Happy to update the default config used in electron-builder, but I'm guessing it'll require semver checks on the electronVersion as to what libs are deprecated or no longer required. So getting that clarity upfront will make any changes here more streamlined of a discussion

So I am now asking here: What are the exact library requirements for an Electron app on Linux?

### Proposed Solution

Please provide a list of dependencies needed for Electron apps on Linux.

### Alternatives Considered

Went with the defaults of electron-builder, but this results in the application not being able to install on RHEL10.

### Additional Information

_No response_

When using `--headless` mode the context menus from Trays don't display. You can still interact with the buttons inside the context menu, their events fire, but they're completely invisible.

nodes.title: Keys stuck when switching between Gnome Workspaces with key combination
nodes.body:
### Electron Version

37.6.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

Fedora 43

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

N/A

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

Im switching between Gnome Workspaces. Im using the default key combination Super + Page Up/Down but have also tried other combinations like Super + Alt + Arrow Left/Right or custom ones.

### Actual Behavior

When i'm switching between Workspaces to VS Code with the key combination, the Page Up/Down (or whatever key im using) gets stuck and i always jump to the top/bottom of the current opened window or when im using the Super + Alt + Arrow Left/Right combination my cursor always travels to the left/right until another key on the keyboard is pressed.

Seems like the Super key does not release after workspace switching.

This does not happen when running VS Code in native Wayland mode, only happens when VS Code runs under XWayland.

**VS Code specs:**

Commit: ac4cbdf48759c7d8c3eb91ffe6bb04316e263c57
Date: 2025-11-11T16:02:25.943Z
Electron: 37.7.0
ElectronBuildId: 12597478
Chromium: 138.0.7204.251
Node.js: 22.20.0
V8: 13.8.258.32-electron.0
OS: Linux x64 6.17.7-300.fc43.x86_64

**Fedora specs:**
OS: Fedora 43
Desktop: GNOME 49
Session: Wayland

### Additional Information

Workaround: start VS Code via `code --ozone-platform-hint=wayland` then im not running into this issue

nodes.title: Modal BrowserWindow: multiple show() calls leave parent disabled after close (refcount issue)

nodes.diff:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.1.2

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Version 10.0.26200.6899]

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.1.0

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When a modal BrowserWindow is created with a parent and modal: true:

1. The parent window should be disabled while the modal is shown.
2. After the modal is closed, the parent should become fully usable again (interactive, focusable),
3. This should hold even if show() has been called more than once on the modal (for example: once immediately, once in ready-to-show).

### Actual Behavior

If show() is called more than once on the modal window, closing the modal leaves the parent in a permanently disabled state:

- The parent cannot be interacted with (no mouse or keyboard interaction).
- It behaves as if a modal is still open and blocking it, even though the modal window is closed.

If, instead, I call hide() before close(), the parent becomes usable again. That suggests a reference-count mismatch for modal children on the parent window.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/gdavidkov/64ed0deb5c169e5a57de4e152be0e1b7

### Additional Information

Every call to Show() on a modal window increments the parent’s num_modal_children_, but the count is only decremented in Hide(). Close() does not adjust this counter.

So if show() is called multiple times on the same modal window, the parent’s num_modal_children_ can remain > 0 after the modal is closed, leaving the parent disabled.

This feels related to the changes in:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48770?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

[https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865](https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48865?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

and is similar in effect to the older issue:

[https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768](https://github.com/electron/electron/issues/8768?utm_source=chatgpt.com)

Workaround

Ensure that either:

- show() is called only once on the modal, or
- Call hide() before close():
 This brings the parent back to a usable state.

nodes.title: Electron 39.2.0 crashes with SIGTRAP when launched via Playwright inspector
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a bug report that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Electron Version

39.2.0

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Other Linux

### Operating System Version

  Fedora 42 (Linux 6.17.7)

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

39.1.2

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When launching an Electron application via Playwright's electron.launch() API (which uses the inspector protocol with --inspect=0 flag), the application should start successfully and remain running for automated testing.


### Actual Behavior

The Electron process crashes immediately with SIGTRAP signal after the debugger attaches:

```
  <launched> pid=366007
  [err] Debugger listening on ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] For help, see: https://nodejs.org/en/docs/inspector
  <ws connecting> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  <ws connected> ws://127.0.0.1:40361/...
  [err] Debugger attached.
  <ws disconnected> code=1006 reason=
  <kill>
  <will force kill>
  <process did exit: exitCode=null, signal=SIGTRAP>
```

This causes all Playwright-based E2E tests to fail.


### Testcase Gist URL

_No response_

### Additional Information

#### Steps To Reproduce

  1. Create a minimal Electron application
  2. Install Playwright: npm install --save-dev playwright@1.56.1
  3. Create a test file that launches Electron via Playwright:

     ```javascript
     const { _electron: electron } = require('playwright');
     const path = require('path');
     
     async function test() {
       const electronApp = await electron.launch({
         args: [
           path.join(__dirname, 'main.js'),
           '--no-sandbox',
           '--disable-gpu'
         ]
       });
   
       // Process crashes before reaching here
       await electronApp.close();
     }
   
     test();
     ```

  4. Run with Electron 39.2.0: Process crashes with SIGTRAP
  5. Downgrade to Electron 39.1.2: Process launches successfully

#### Root Cause Analysis

The issue appears to be caused by PR #48703 ("Automatically focus DevTools when element is inspected or breakpoint is triggered"), which was included in 39.2.0.

When Playwright connects via the inspector protocol, the new automatic DevTools activation logic tries to activate/focus a DevTools window that doesn't exist in the Playwright test environment, causing the crash.


#### Impact

This regression breaks all Playwright-based testing for applications that upgrade to Electron 39.2.0, affecting CI/CD pipelines and automated testing workflows.

safeStorage does not seem to work without DBUS enabled - incompatible with proper secure sandboxing of applications
nodes.body:
### Preflight Checklist

- [ ] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project.
- [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to.
- [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success.

### Problem Description

Originating issue: Element Desktop https://github.com/element-hq/element-web/issues/32008 

I was forwarded to upstream as this appears an Electron issue: About 1 1/2 years ago, I noticed that I could no longer launch Element Desktop with my tried & tested firejail configuration. While it launched, it failed to read the configuration / authentication data from the jail.
It turned out that for this to work, I was no longer able to block DBUS (`env DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS=none firejail [..]`)

I consider this a security risk because: When DBUS is available, applications that launch other applications (in my case: Element Desktop launching a web browser for authentication to homeservers) will launch them outside the jailed context, giving them full access to the user home directory. In the case of a web browser, this exposes the user space to security flaws exploited by any website that is opened from an unjailed browser.

When DBUS is disabled, applications are launched within the same jailed context, and this security risk goes away / becomes acceptable.

In the referenced issue, I was informed that this likely results from the use of electron's safeStorage, and sure enough, as soon as I used the option to disable safeStorage (`~/.config/Element/electron-config.json`, setting: `safeStorageBackend: "plaintext"`), I could again launch the application in a jailed configuration with DBUS disabled.


### Proposed Solution

I would like to kindly request that the electron team investigates whether it is possible to make safeStorage work *without* DBUS available in a sandbox (e.g. firejail), thereby enabling both safeStorage *and* keeping further applications launched from a jailed application inside that same jail.

### Alternatives Considered

Currently working: disable DBUS but accept that safeStorage is not available.

### Additional Information

_No response_

### Electron Version

### What operating system(s) are you using?

Windows

### Operating System Version

Windows 11 Business, 25H2, build: 26200.7171

### What arch are you using?

x64

### Last Known Working Electron version

_No response_

### Does the issue also appear in Chromium / Google Chrome?

No

### Expected Behavior

When initializing a search via findInPage and cycling through it via { forward: true } (from the webcontents) for an embedded PDF viewer in an iframe the results returned by the found-in-page should properly increment the activeMatchOrdinal and highlight the next result correctly

### Actual Behavior

Setup:
- Webpage with an embedded PDF viewer in an iframe
- Initializing a search via the webconents search-in-page for items that are present in the page/pdf and cycle them through { forward: true } argument
- Subscribe to the webcontents 'found-in-page' event and log the results

Two different behaviors seem to occur:
- If a 'result' is found and highlighted outside of the PDF file - for an example in the title, it fails to move the 'activeMatchOrdinal' from outside of the embedded file to the file results
- if a 'result' is found on further pages in the file (i.e. results are present outside of the visible page), instead of increasing the increment - the 'results' property returned by the event is getting incremented

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/tbratanov/5e9d1d5c0b8f0ff4ce99d45dee5f8b74

### Additional Information

_No response_

nodes.title: Make it easy to use SF Symbols in macOS menu items
nodes.body: ### Preflight Checklist - [x] I have read the [Contributing Guidelines](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) for this project. - [x] I agree to follow the [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/electron/electron/blob/main/CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md) that this project adheres to. - [x] I have searched the [issue tracker](https://www.github.com/electron/electron/issues) for a feature request that matches the one I want to file, without success. ### Problem Description In macOS Tahoe, menu items for context menus, tray icon menus, application menus, etc. can have icons next to them. Here are Apple's design docs for the feature: https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/menus#Icons It would be great if it was possible to show SF Symbol icons there in the right size and with the right settings in one line of code. Based on my experimentation, I can replicate the native look by saving symbols from the [SF Symbols app](https://developer.apple.com/sf-symbols/) with the following settings: - Font: SF Pro - Font weight: Semibold - Rendering mode: Monochrome - Color: Black (100%) - Background: Default - Point size: 13 - Symbol scale: Small (Right-click the icon, select "Copy Image As…", then select PNG) Then I load them using `nativeImage.createFromPath()`. This replicates the native look. ### Proposed Solution It would be great if there was a one-line solution to load an SF Symbol with the correct settings (see above) so that we can set it as `menuItem.icon`. This work could build on https://github.com/electron/electron/pull/48203. It would need to extend that logic to load semibold icons. ### Alternatives Considered Alternatively, developers will need to save every image manually. This doesn't make sense. ### Additional Information CC @TheCommieAxolotl

This worked fine on Electon 37 with wayland so I imagine it has something to do with Chromium ozone changes.

### Testcase Gist URL

https://gist.github.com/Sytten/75ace5d29b59d37e3f6ae382d1c89f3e

### Additional Information

If you run this gist on 37 you will see the window open, but all versions more recent will not show the window on wayland.

### Problem Description

I use Ubuntu with [KeepassXC](https://github.com/keepassxreboot/keepassxc) instead of KWallet as the secret store.
Currently, for `safeStorage` on Linux (see [documentation](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/safe-storage)):
`Options currently supported are kwallet, kwallet5, kwallet6 and gnome-libsecret, but more may be available in future versions of Electron`



### Proposed Solution

Add support for [KeepassXC](https://github.com/keepassxreboot/keepassxc) for `safeStorage`
